extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent applicants/practitioners, and stakeholders concerned with inventorship for AI-assisted inventions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether human contributions to inventions that involved AI are sufficiently significant to qualify human(s) as named inventor(s) on a U.S. patent or patent application. Focuses on how examiners and applicants should analyze inventorship when AI systems also contributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human 'significant contribution' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent protection may be sought for inventions in which a human provided a significant contribution to the invention; to secure patent protection, there must be at least one named human inventor who meets that requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Builds on the existing inventorship framework and the 'significant contribution' test from Pannu v. Iolab Corp. The key question is whether the human named on a patent made a significant enough contribution to be named as an inventor. The guidance emphasizes that at least one human's actions must be shown to rise to the level of inventorship and be listed as an inventor on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the Pannu 'significant contribution' test
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should apply the Federal Circuit's 1998 Pannu significant contribution test (Pannu v. Iolab Corp., 155 F.3d 1344 (Fed. Cir. 1998)) when assessing inventorship in AI-assisted inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance builds on the test examiners have been applying for decades; it does not substitute a new inventorship standard but instructs how to use that established framework in AI contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat AI-assisted inventions as categorically unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-assisted inventions are not categorically unpatentable; use of AI in the inventive process does not automatically bar patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO 'embraces the use of AI in innovation' and will continue to assess patent applications on existing patentability grounds while applying the inventorship guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-contribution analysis centers on human acts, not hypothetical humanized-AI acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of considering whether contributions of the AI system would rise to the same level of inventorship if made by a human, the inquiry is whether the human named made a significant enough contribution to be an inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reframing focuses analysis on the evidence of human contributions rather than analogizing AI actions to human inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing a problem and presenting it to AI is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely recognizing a problem and presenting that problem to an AI system is not enough to establish someone as an inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance uses illustrative examples showing that simple problem identification and submission to an AI does not satisfy the significant-contribution requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing prompts can be a significant contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual made a significant contribution through the construction of a prompt, that could be sufficient to qualify as an inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance expressly notes that prompt construction, when sufficiently creative or contributory, may meet the significant contribution threshold; examples are provided to illustrate when prompt work rises to inventorship-level contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Intellectual domination' over an AI system is not alone sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining 'intellectual domination' over an AI system, by itself, does not make a person an inventor of any inventions created through that AI system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO explains that controlling or directing an AI tool requires more substantive, inventive contribution to qualify for inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO presumption that named inventors are actual inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will continue to presume that the named inventor(s) in an application are the actual inventor(s); applicants remain responsible for meeting their existing duties to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship questions will be raised by an examiner only in rare instances where the file record or extrinsic evidence indicates that one or more named inventors may not have invented the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new general AI-use disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is not implementing any new requirement to disclose the use of AI in applications at this time, beyond what is required in rare circumstances by existing USPTO rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although AI is increasingly used, the guidance takes an iterative approach and does not broadly mandate disclosure of AI involvement; the agency will continue to engage with stakeholders about possible future updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other patentability requirements remain applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: This inventorship guidance does not entitle inventors to a patent; applications must still meet all other criteria for patentability including patent eligibility, novelty, and nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO is assessing how patent eligibility, novelty, and nonobviousness apply in view of AI and is preparing related guidance; inventorship is necessary but not sufficient for patent grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance excludes consideration of whether IP was used to train AI
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance does not take into consideration whether any intellectual property was utilized in the training of any AI systems used as part of the inventive process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent grants exclusive rights to an invention but does not confer the right to use another's IP; applicants must secure whatever other IP rights they need (e.g., when inventing on top of another patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners instructed with illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance provides instructions to examiners on determining correct inventor(s) when humans and AI systems both contributed, and includes specific hypothetical examples illustrating different AI roles and how inventorship should be analyzed in each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO published specific examples to assist examiners and applicants in understanding application of the guidance; the agency will engage publicly and iteratively refine guidance based on feedback.
